articles.title: Structured output comes to the API
articles.summary: OpenAI introduced a way to constrain compatible model responses to a supplied JSON Schema.
articles.what: OpenAI introduced Structured Outputs for compatible API models.
articles.why: Schema adherence reduces parsing failures in workflows that pass responses to other software.
articles.context: Valid JSON can still omit fields or use unexpected types.
articles.action: OpenAI added constrained decoding against a supported JSON Schema.
articles.result: Applications can request schema-conforming responses and still need to handle refusals and incomplete responses.

source.title: Introducing Structured Outputs in the API

articles.title: Spark 4.0 changes SQL defaults
articles.summary: The major Spark release enables ANSI SQL mode by default and introduces migration considerations for existing jobs.
articles.why: Queries relying on permissive casts can behave differently after an upgrade.
articles.context: Some existing pipelines depend on earlier SQL error handling.
articles.action: Spark 4.0 enables ANSI SQL mode by default.
articles.result: Teams can check casts, overflow and migration notes before promoting an upgraded job.

articles.title: The Fed lowers its target range
articles.summary: The FOMC reduced the federal funds target range by 25 basis points as it assessed increasing employment risks.
articles.what: The FOMC cut its target range to 4.00–4.25%.
articles.why: The committee cited a shift in the balance of risks, including rising downside risks to employment.
articles.context: The committee described inflation as somewhat elevated and job gains as slower.
articles.action: It lowered the target range by a quarter percentage point.
articles.result: The new range took effect under the policy decision and further moves remained data-dependent.

articles.title: How automatic differentiation works
articles.summary: A journal survey explains forward and reverse accumulation, including why reverse mode suits many machine-learning workloads.
articles.what: The authors surveyed automatic differentiation and its uses in machine learning.
articles.why: Picking the right accumulation mode depends on how many inputs and outputs a computation has.
articles.context: Optimisation often requires derivatives of programs with many parameters.
articles.action: The paper compares differentiation techniques and explains forward and reverse accumulation.
articles.result: It gives readers a framework for choosing a derivative method for their workload.
articles.formula: For L(θ) = θ², the gradient is dL/dθ = 2θ.

source.authors: A. G. Baydin, B. A. Pearlmutter, A. A. Radul and J. M. Siskind
source.title: Automatic Differentiation in Machine Learning: a Survey

articles.title: FlashAttention-2 reorganises GPU work
articles.summary: The ICLR paper improves work partitioning for exact attention and reports gains on its tested GPU workloads.
articles.what: Tri Dao presented a revised FlashAttention algorithm at ICLR 2024.
articles.why: The allocation of work across GPU threads and blocks affects utilisation.
articles.context: The first FlashAttention implementation still left room to improve GPU utilisation.
articles.action: The revision reduces certain non-matrix operations and changes GPU work partitioning.
articles.result: The paper reports higher throughput in its benchmarks. Applying that result elsewhere requires testing the target hardware.

source.title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning

articles.title: PostgreSQL 17 revisits vacuum memory
articles.summary: PostgreSQL 17 introduced a revised memory structure for vacuum and other performance changes for operators to evaluate.
articles.why: Vacuum memory demands affect database maintenance and resource planning.
articles.context: Operators balance vacuum performance with other workloads that need memory.
articles.action: The project changed the memory structure used by vacuum.
articles.result: The release reports lower vacuum memory consumption relative to earlier versions. Measure it against your tables and settings.

articles.title: The Fed holds rates in June
articles.summary: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range at 4.25–4.50% at its June 2025 meeting.
articles.what: The FOMC held the target range at 4.25–4.50%.
articles.why: The decision provides a dated policy baseline for scenarios and comparisons.
articles.context: The committee assessed developments against its inflation and employment goals.
articles.action: It maintained the prevailing target range.
articles.result: US monetary policy retained the same target range at that meeting.

articles.title: The DeepSeek-V3 technical report
articles.summary: The first arXiv version describes a mixture-of-experts language model and reports the authors’ evaluations.
articles.what: DeepSeek posted its V3 technical report to arXiv.
articles.why: The report provides training and architecture details readers can compare with other systems.
articles.context: Mixture-of-experts designs activate a subset of parameters for each token.
articles.action: The authors described their architecture, training approach and evaluation setup.
articles.result: The cited arXiv version presents author-reported results. The measurements depend on that report’s setup.
